structured_output.nutrition_advice: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine a targeted antibody with a potent cytotoxic payload. While they can attack tumors effectively, off-target effects or payload release may also trigger gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, marrow, or lung toxicity. The core nutrition principles are: higher protein, easy digestion, small frequent meals, and side-effect-specific adjustments. Because ADC targets may be broadly expressed in the gastrointestinal tract, or because the gut lining turns over quickly, nausea, diarrhea, and reduced intake are common. Use small, frequent, bland meals; avoid greasy, fried, and spicy foods; and aim for 5 to 6 eating moments per day without overfilling. Prioritize steamed fish, poached chicken breast, tofu, steamed egg, and vitamin-rich gourd vegetables for higher-protein, easier-to-digest choices. If diarrhea becomes significant, watch for dehydration and electrolyte loss and use oral rehydration solution, or lightly salted rice broth. Avoid milk and dairy because lactose can worsen gut burden. If nausea is severe, avoid large amounts of fluid during meals and move soups and other liquid foods to at least 30 minutes before or after eating. For the next few days, aim for lower-salt, moderate-protein, low-stimulant meals. Steamed fish, chicken breast, tofu, oatmeal, soft rice, and cooked vegetables fit better than energy drinks, strong coffee, or very salty take-out foods.

diet_tips.title: Spread fluids through the day
diet_tips.detail: Small frequent drinks work better than waiting until you are very thirsty.

diet_tips.title: Scale back stimulants
diet_tips.detail: Strong coffee, energy drinks, and excess alcohol can make palpitations feel worse.

diet_tips.title: Trim sodium a little more
diet_tips.detail: BP is already drifting, so lower-salt meals give the medication more room to work.

diet_tips.title: Track food and symptoms together
diet_tips.detail: Some people notice palpitations cluster after large meals, poor sleep, or caffeine.

diet_tips.title: Small frequent meals
diet_tips.detail: Aim for 5 to 6 eating moments per day instead of one or two heavy meals to reduce nausea, bloating, and post-meal discomfort.

diet_tips.title: Higher-protein and easy to digest
diet_tips.detail: Steamed fish, poached chicken breast, tofu, and steamed egg are practical ADC-treatment protein staples.

diet_tips.title: Replace fluids and salt during diarrhea
diet_tips.detail: Significant diarrhea causes fluid and electrolyte loss, so use oral rehydration solution or lightly salted rice broth.

diet_tips.title: Pause dairy if diarrhea is active
diet_tips.detail: Lactose in milk and dairy can add to gut burden when diarrhea is already present.

diet_tips.title: Separate larger liquids from meals if nausea is strong
diet_tips.detail: Move soups and other liquid foods to at least 30 minutes before or after eating when nausea is severe.

health_guidance.summary: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine a targeted antibody with a potent cytotoxic payload. While they can attack tumors effectively, off-target effects or payload release may also trigger gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, marrow, or lung toxicity. The core nutrition principles are: higher protein, easy digestion, small frequent meals, and side-effect-specific adjustments. This page is best read as an early cardiac signal that needs to be objectified quickly, not something to push through and ignore.
